title: Animal Mech Lab
reference_role: PS1 simplification and rendering only; all four designs are new concepts.

concepts.name: Stag Beetle
concepts.silhouette: A low, broad torso; two blunt horn-like sensor vanes; split shell shoulder and back masses; short sturdy legs.
concepts.purpose: Test a compact heavy silhouette whose identity comes from the shell and head outline.
concepts.palette: Charcoal, muted oxide orange, warm gray joints.
concepts.design: Concept A — STAG BEETLE heavy biped. Design a squat but adult-proportioned armored core with an unusually wide compact torso, a small head tucked low between huge angular shoulders, two short broad squared sensor prongs that recall stag-beetle mandibles above the head, and a pair of broad trapezoid shell plates that wrap the shoulder/back silhouette like split elytra. The shell shapes must be flat-sided wedges, never rounded carapaces. A short narrow waist, sturdy thick thighs and short broad wedge shins create a planted heavy-machine stance. Forearms are substantial but expose the five-digit block hands. Main colors charcoal armor with a few large muted oxide-orange shell faces, dark square joints and warm-gray hands. No actual beetle head or extra insect limbs; no giant ornamental antlers.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one individual concept image for an animal-inspired low-poly mech exploration.
Input image role: the supplied gray mech is a STYLE AND SIMPLICITY REFERENCE ONLY. Match its broad flat faces, extremely sparse detail, simple joints and early PlayStation 3D game-model appearance. Invent a substantially new silhouette and proportions for the animal concept below.

Primary request: an original military bipedal mech in the industrial design spirit of the original PlayStation-era Armored Core games, taking structural inspiration from an animal. The animal informs the arrangement and outline of armor, body proportions and mechanical balance. It remains a piloted armored machine with a compact sensor head, torso core, waist, two articulated arms, two legs and compact booster housings.

CRITICAL HAND DESIGN: BOTH hands have exactly FIVE INDIVIDUAL DIGITS: FOUR distinct fingers in a row plus ONE visibly separate opposable thumb. Use a simple block palm, four separate long cuboid fingers of slightly varied lengths, each made from only two rectangular segments, and a short two-block thumb attached to the side. Make clear air gaps between every finger. Pose both hands relaxed and open with palms angled partly toward the camera, fingers spread slightly and completely visible, away from thighs. Make the fingers large enough to count. Fingers must have the SAME deliberately crude angular geometry as the body, without rounded knuckles or intricate joints. No mittens, fused grippers, pincers, claws replacing fingers, three-finger hands or six digits.

Style/medium: render a deliberately primitive low-poly 3D game model. Main armor shells are very simple box, wedge and low-sided prism forms, just a few broad polygon faces per piece, flat shading and solid colors, occasional broad painted blocks only. Simple square hinges. Keep the fewest forms that express the unique silhouette. No fine panel lines, tiny bevels, greebles, rivets, hoses, pistons, realistic metal, weathering, elaborate textures, wireframe overlay or triangle-pattern textures. No voxel aesthetic, chibi proportions, smooth modern toy render, organic flesh, fur, feathers or decorative animal costume.

Composition: ONE mech, full body from helmet to feet, front three-quarter angle about 25 degrees so torso and limb depth read but both hands are visible; neutral grounded standing stance, arms slightly away from torso, entire head, silhouette extremities, hands and feet in frame with white margins. Neutral even light, pure white backdrop, no scenery, no text, logos, labels, inset views, diagrams or watermark. Portrait composition about 3:4. Empty hands, no guns, shields, carried props or weapon mounts that obscure the silhouette.

concepts.name: Mantis
concepts.silhouette: A tiny triangular sensor head, narrow torso, raised shoulder wedges, long folded forearm shells and long angular legs.
concepts.purpose: Test an insect-inspired light frame while preserving useful five-fingered manipulators.
concepts.palette: Muted olive, bone-gray blocks, charcoal joints.
concepts.design: Concept B — MANTIS tall light biped. An extremely narrow vertical chest and small triangular wedge sensor head sit between two elevated blade-shaped shoulder armor wedges. Long slim upper arms lead into long faceted forearm armor which folds back alongside the elbow, recalling the folded profile of mantis forelimbs, while ending in fully functional FIVE-DIGIT humanoid block hands. The forearms are armor shells, not sickle blades or claws. Narrow waist, very long thin mechanical legs, strongly angular bent knees, small planted wedge feet, and two thin flat booster fins along the upper back. Distinctively tall, sparse and triangular in silhouette. Main colors muted olive-green armor, a few broad bone-gray blocks, charcoal hinges and bone-gray fingers. Just a few large faces per armor shell; no insect face or extra limbs.

concepts.name: Raven
concepts.silhouette: A forward wedge sensor head, swept triangular shoulder planes, compact chest, long reverse-joint legs and flat heel fins.
concepts.purpose: Test an agile avian silhouette through armor direction and leg geometry.
concepts.palette: Blue-black, slate gray, restrained amber sensor.
concepts.design: Concept C — RAVEN agile reverse-joint biped. A small forward-projecting beak-like sensor wedge is recessed under a broad angular collar. Two single flat swept-back triangular shoulder plates evoke folded wings without actual wings or feathers. A short forward-leaning chest, thin waist, compact pelvis, long digitigrade reverse-joint legs with high mechanical hocks and simple broad two-block wedge feet create an avian balance. Two short flat tail-like stabilizer fins extend behind the pelvis, and two compact rectangular boosters sit behind the torso. Ordinary useful articulated arms with visible FIVE-DIGIT block hands; no arm wings or talon hands. Blue-black broad armor faces, a few slate-gray contrast planes, pale-gray simple fingers and a tiny muted amber rectangular sensor. Silhouette must feel built from a few crisp triangles and boxes, not a bird-shaped toy.

concepts.name: Hound
concepts.silhouette: A low wedge head, two short sensor fins, forward chest, tapered hips, thick forearms and long runner legs.
concepts.purpose: Test a lean pursuit frame through weight distribution and tapered masses.
concepts.palette: Dusty sand, dark graphite, restrained rust-red blocks.
concepts.design: Concept D — HOUND pursuit biped. A small low wedge sensor head with two short upright trapezoid antenna fins sits ahead of a forward-projecting compact armored chest. Suggest a hound through a deep narrow ribcage-like torso, very tucked thin waist, tapered high hips and long springy mechanical runner legs with high rear hocks. Keep the helmet abstract and industrial, no literal dog muzzle, face or eyes. Sloping broad shoulder wedges and oversized blunt rectangular forearm gauntlets balance the lean rear body. Feet are short long-toed industrial wedges, not paws. Two modest squared booster pods follow the back's slope. Both empty human-layout FIVE-DIGIT hands stay clearly visible below gauntlets. Dusty sand broad armor planes, dark graphite joints and a few large rust-red accent blocks; light-gray fingers. Entirely angular flat simple construction, no animal tail, fur, claws or extra legs.
